abstract: Ardisia tchimbele sp. nov. (Primulaceae) an erect, branching shrub, is described from the forests downstream of Tchimbele, a hydroelectric installation in the Crystal Mountains, Gabon that supplies Libreville, the capital with energy. The new species is based on three specimens collected in the 1980s and 1990s. It keys out and has similarities with a taxon informally described in 1979 by Taton as Ardisia sp. 1, also from the Crystal Mts and which is slightly discordant morphologically. The new species is considered threatened by the risk of flooding of its habitat from further hydroelectric projects and is provisionally assessed as Critically Endangered using the 2012 IUCN standard. We offer as context a short review of the vegetation, topography and plant diversity of the Crystal Mountains of Gabon.
